chunks: From him, from Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hafsh, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to freeing the child of fornication."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a child born from fornication in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that the child of a concubine or slave woman who commits fornication is not disqualified from manumission, affirming their legal status as property capable of being freed. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the *zina* of the mother does not impede the father's or owner's ability to grant her freedom, distinguishing it from other lineage complications. The ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic manumission laws regarding children of mixed-status unions.
